description: As winter approaches the generation at Hydro stations situated at north-east part of eastern region and Bhutan start depleting. Further, the surplus power that North Eastern Region injects in ER grid decreases, due to depletion of hydro sources in that region, and subsequently NER starts drawing power from ER to meet its demand. The demand in Northern Region almost remains flat and high. The 400 kV Malda-Purnea D/C is utilized for exporting power to NER and NR besides meeting the demand of North Bihar and part of North Bengal. This high export scenario to NER and NR and less generation at Northeastern part of ER, causes severe overloading of this line. Prolonged outage of 400 kV Purnea-Biharsariff D/C and 400 kV Patna –Kishanganj D/C line has further aggravated the loading of above line. However by maintaining the power flow through Agra-BNC HVDC line towards NER, loading on this line was controlled.
notes: NLDC quarterly operational feedback issued 2017-04; re_related is a keyword flag

description: 220 kV side of 400 /220kV substation at Maithon is connected with Dhanbad and Kalyaneswari. Kalyaneswari in turn caters to loads of Kalipahari, Burnpur, Kumardubi etc. in DVC. description: As winter approaches the generation at Hydro stations situated at north-east part of eastern region and Bhutan start depleting. Thus the excess hydro power that North Eastern Region used to inject in ER grid decreases and subsequently NER starts drawing power from ER to meet its demand. The demand in Northern Region almost remains flat and high. The 400 kV Malda-Purnea D/C is approximately 170 Km long line. The power flows through it during winter season is normally utilized to meet the demand of North Bengal and contains exported power to NER and NR. This high export scenario to NER and NR and less generation at Northeast Part of ER causes a severe overloading of this line. Prolonged outage of 400 kV Purnea- Biharsariff D/C and 400 kV Patna –Kishanganj D/C line has further aggravated the loading of above line. However with keeping the power flow direction in Agra-BNC HVDC line in direction NR to NER loading on this line is controlled.
notes: NLDC quarterly operational feedback issued 2017-01; re_related is a keyword flag

description: Maithon is a major load center of DVC, and power generated from MPL has a natural tendency to flow through MPL–Maithon line, because it has less impedance (short length line) compared to MPL- Ranchi line. Moreover, injection of power from WR at Ranchi further aggravates the situation as the power flow from Ranchi to MPL through 400kV Ranchi-MPL D/C gets added to the generation of MPL, and the resultant power gets evacuated through MPL- Maithon D/c line, so due to these reasons sometimes 400kV MPL- Maithon flow exceeded 450-500 MW / ckt and (n-1) security criterion got violated. However, after commissioning of 400kV N.Ranchi- Chandwa-Gaya D/C Quad moose line on 10.7.2016, loading of this line had reduced significantly, and most of the time it was within limit compared to last quarter.

element: 400/220 kV 1 x 500 + 1x 315 MVA ICT at Maithon
description: 220 kV side of 400 /220kV substation at Maithon is connected with Dhanbad and Kalyaneswari. Further from Dhanbad connectivity is there to Giridih, Nimiaghat, Putki etc. besides Chandrapura TPS. From Kalyaneswari loads of Kalipahari, Burnpur, Kumardubi etc. are supplied. In addition, JUSNL also draws around 80-100 MW at its Dumka S/Stn through 220kV Maithon-Dumka D/C tie line. As these S/Stns are situated in coal belt having major industrial and mining load and the generation of nearby thermal power plant connected at 220 kV level was also low and DVC had to draw heavy power through Maithon ICT to meet these loads. Thus (n-1) security got violated. However, after replacement of 315 MVA ICT-I with 500 MVA on 16- 09-16, loading on the other ICT-II had reduced significantly. But tripping of the 500 MVA ICT could have led to loss of the other 315 MVA ICT on overload. The problem is expected to be resolved after replacement of remaining 315 MVA ICT by another 500 MVA.

element: 220 kV Budhipadar- Lapanga D/C, 220 kV Budhipadar Vedanta D/C and 220 kV Rourkela- Tarkera D/C
description: Constraints: These lines are not N-1 compliant. This issue has been observed with very high injection from Vedanta Captive plant (250-300 MW) on a persistent basis. Further, it has been enhanced with the retirement of 220 kV TTPS power plant in the Odhisa system. Also, parallel bunching of 400/220 kV ICTs at Rourkela (2 X 630 MVA) have led to a low impedance path which is leading to higher loading on only evacuation lines i.e., 220 kV Rourkela-Tarkera D/C planned from the Rourkela substation. Situation gets worsens with high drawl by RSP which is relatively higher this year in comparison to last year. Reliability of equipment at Budhipadar S/S got reduced due to ageing. Remedial Action Plan: 1. Reconductoring of 220 kV Rourkela-Tarkera D/C with HTLS conductor 2. SPS has been designed to control the power flow through 220 kV Rourkela – Tarkera D/C. 3. Reducing injection from Vedanta CPP by Odisha SLDC.

description: Constraints: At present power generated at Teesta-III, Dikchu, Chujachen, Jorthang along with Teesta-V is pooled at Rangpo and evaculated through 400 kV Rangpo- Binaguri D/C.
